title: 茅屋为秋风所破歌
title_en: Song of My Thatched Hut Torn Apart by the Autumn Wind
author: 杜甫

form.en: song in the old style, mostly seven characters a line

text_note.zh: 这里用的是现在统编版语文课本的文字。古籍本子有几处字不一样：“渡江”作“度江”，“沉塘坳”作“沈塘坳”，“南村”作“南邨”，“倚杖”作“倚仗”，“娇儿”作“骄儿”，“床头屋漏”作“床床屋漏”。“度”和“渡”、“沈”和“沉”、“邨”和“村”在古代是相通的写法，意思一样。
text_note.en: This follows the text in today's national school textbook. Some old editions differ in a few places: du (to cross) is written with a different character, chen (to sink) and cun (village) use old forms, yi zhang (lean on a staff) has a look-alike character, jiao er (dear child) is written with a character meaning 'spoiled child', and chuang tou (by the bed) appears as chuang chuang (bed after bed). The old forms of du, chen and cun meant the same thing.

readings.zh: 号：这里读 háo，大声叫、呼啸。不读 hào。
readings.en: hào is the usual reading, but here it is háo: to howl, to roar.

readings.zh: 重：这里读 chóng，表示“层”。三重茅就是三层茅草。
readings.en: Read chóng here, meaning a layer. Not zhòng (heavy).

readings.zh: 坳：课本读 ào。有的旧字典注 āo。
readings.en: The textbook reads ào. Some older dictionaries give āo.

readings.zh: 为：读 wéi，意思是“做”。为盗贼就是做强盗、小偷。
readings.en: Read wéi here: to act as, to be.

readings.zh: 丧：读 sāng。丧乱指战乱、死亡和流离的苦难。不读 sàng。
readings.en: Read sāng here, as in sāng luàn, the death and chaos of war.

readings.zh: 见：同“现”，读 xiàn，出现的意思。
readings.en: Here this character stands for xiàn, to appear, so it is read xiàn, not jiàn.

glosses.zh: 秋高：秋天天空又高又远。
glosses.en: qiū gāo: in autumn the sky looks high and far away.

glosses.zh: 怒号：大声吼叫。这里形容风刮得很猛，呼呼作响。
glosses.en: nù háo: to roar with anger. Here the wind howls loudly.

glosses.zh: 三重茅：好几层茅草。三重，几层，不一定正好三层。茅，茅草，一种长长的野草，可以用来盖屋顶。
glosses.en: sān chóng máo: several layers of thatch. Máo is long grass that was used to cover roofs.

glosses.zh: 洒江郊：散落在江对岸的野地上。郊，野外。
glosses.en: sǎ jiāng jiāo: scattered on the open land along the river.

glosses.zh: 挂罥：挂着、缠绕着。罥，缠住、挂住。
glosses.en: guà juàn: to hang and get tangled. Juàn means to get caught on something.

glosses.zh: 长林梢：高高的树林的树梢上。
glosses.en: cháng lín shāo: the tips of the tall trees.

glosses.zh: 飘转：在空中打着转飘落。
glosses.en: piāo zhuǎn: to float and spin in the air.

glosses.zh: 塘坳：低洼积水的地方，像水坑、池塘。坳，低洼的地方。
glosses.en: táng ào: a low wet place, like a pond or a puddle.

glosses.zh: 忍能：竟然忍心这样。
glosses.en: rěn néng: could bear to, had the heart to.

glosses.zh: 对面：当着面。
glosses.en: duì miàn: right in front of me.

glosses.zh: 公然：毫不掩饰地，明目张胆地。
glosses.en: gōng rán: openly, without hiding it.

glosses.zh: 入竹去：跑进竹林里去了。
glosses.en: rù zhú qù: ran off into the bamboo grove.

glosses.zh: 唇焦口燥：嘴唇干裂，口干舌燥。
glosses.en: chún jiāo kǒu zào: lips cracked, mouth dry.

glosses.zh: 呼不得：喊也喊不住。
glosses.en: hū bù dé: shouting did no good.

glosses.zh: 倚杖：拄着拐杖。
glosses.en: yǐ zhàng: leaning on a walking stick.

glosses.zh: 俄顷：一会儿，不久。
glosses.en: é qǐng: a moment later.

glosses.zh: 云墨色：云变得像墨一样黑。
glosses.en: yún mò sè: the clouds turned black as ink.

glosses.zh: 漠漠：灰蒙蒙的，一片昏暗。
glosses.en: mò mò: grey and dim, everywhere the same.

glosses.zh: 向昏黑：渐渐黑下来。向，接近、快要。
glosses.en: xiàng hūn hēi: growing dark. Xiàng means getting close to.

glosses.zh: 布衾：布做的被子。衾，被子。
glosses.en: bù qīn: a cloth quilt. Qīn means quilt.

glosses.zh: 娇儿：心爱的孩子。
glosses.en: jiāo ér: my dear child.

glosses.zh: 恶卧：睡相不好，乱蹬乱踢。
glosses.en: è wò: sleeping badly, kicking about.

glosses.zh: 踏里裂：把被子里子蹬破了。里，被子的里子，贴着身体的那一面。
glosses.en: tà lǐ liè: kicked a hole in the lining. Lǐ is the inside layer of the quilt.

glosses.zh: 屋漏：屋顶漏雨。
glosses.en: wū lòu: the roof leaks.

glosses.zh: 无干处：没有一块干的地方。
glosses.en: wú gān chù: not one dry spot.

glosses.zh: 雨脚：落到地面的雨点，一条条像脚一样。
glosses.en: yǔ jiǎo: the rain's feet, the streaks of rain hitting the ground.

glosses.zh: 如麻：像一根根麻线那样又密又长。
glosses.en: rú má: thick and close like strands of hemp thread.

glosses.zh: 丧乱：战乱带来的死亡和流离。这里指安史之乱。
glosses.en: sāng luàn: death and chaos from war. Here it means the An Lushan Rebellion.

glosses.zh: 沾湿：被雨淋湿。
glosses.en: zhān shī: soaked by the rain.

glosses.zh: 何由彻：怎样才能熬到天亮。彻，到头，这里指到天亮。
glosses.en: hé yóu chè: how can I get through to dawn? Chè means to the end.

glosses.zh: 安得：怎么能得到。
glosses.en: ān dé: how could I get.

glosses.zh: 广厦：宽大的房子。
glosses.en: guǎng shà: big, roomy houses.

glosses.zh: 大庇：全都遮住、保护起来。庇，遮蔽、保护。
glosses.en: dà bì: to shelter all of them. Bì means to cover and protect.

glosses.zh: 寒士：贫穷的读书人。这里也泛指天下的穷苦人。
glosses.en: hán shì: poor scholars, and more widely, all poor people.

glosses.zh: 俱欢颜：全都开心地笑。俱，都。
glosses.en: jù huān yán: all with happy faces. Jù means all.

glosses.zh: 呜呼：表示感叹的声音，相当于“唉”。
glosses.en: wū hū: a sigh, like 'Ah!' or 'Alas!'

glosses.zh: 突兀：高高耸立的样子。
glosses.en: tū wù: standing tall and high.

glosses.zh: 吾庐：我的茅屋。庐，简陋的房子。
glosses.en: wú lú: my hut. Lú is a simple house.

glosses.zh: 亦足：也心甘情愿。足，满足。
glosses.en: yì zú: I would still be content.

translation.zh: 八月秋高气爽，狂风呼呼地怒吼，
translation.en: In the eighth month the autumn sky is high, and the wind howls in anger.

translation.zh: 把我屋顶上好几层茅草都卷走了。
translation.en: It rips off the layers of thatch from my roof.

translation.zh: 茅草飞过江去，散落在江边的野地上。
translation.en: The thatch flies across the river and scatters on the far bank.

translation.zh: 飞得高的，缠挂在高高的树梢上；
translation.en: The high pieces get tangled in the tops of tall trees.

translation.zh: 飞得低的，打着转沉进了水塘里。
translation.en: The low ones spin down and sink into the ponds.

translation.zh: 南村的一群孩子欺负我年老没力气，
translation.en: A crowd of boys from the south village pick on me, because I am old and weak.

translation.zh: 竟然忍心当着我的面做起贼来。
translation.en: Right in front of me, they act like thieves.

translation.zh: 明目张胆地抱着茅草跑进竹林里去了。
translation.en: Openly they grab the thatch and run off into the bamboo.

translation.zh: 我喊得嘴唇干裂、口干舌燥，也喊不住他们，
translation.en: I shout until my lips crack and my mouth is dry, but it does no good.

translation.zh: 只好回到家，拄着拐杖独自叹气。
translation.en: I come back home, lean on my stick, and sigh to myself.

translation.zh: 不一会儿风停了，云黑得像墨一样，
translation.en: Soon the wind stops, and the clouds turn black as ink.

translation.zh: 秋天的天空灰蒙蒙的，渐渐黑了下来。
translation.en: The autumn sky grows dim and slowly turns dark.

translation.zh: 盖了多年的布被子又冷又硬，像铁一样，
translation.en: My cloth quilt, used for years, is cold and hard as iron.

translation.zh: 孩子睡相不好，把被里蹬破了。
translation.en: My dear child sleeps badly and has kicked a hole in the lining.

translation.zh: 床头屋顶漏雨，没有一块干的地方，
translation.en: The roof leaks above the bed, and not one spot is dry.

translation.zh: 雨点像麻线一样密，一直下个不停。
translation.en: The rain falls thick as hemp threads and never stops.

translation.zh: 自从经历战乱，我就很少能睡好觉，
translation.en: Since the war and its chaos, I have hardly been able to sleep.

translation.zh: 这漫漫长夜浑身湿透，怎样才能熬到天亮！
translation.en: Soaked through on this long night, how can I last until dawn?

translation.zh: 怎样才能得到千万间宽敞的大房子，
translation.en: Oh, if only I could have a million big, roomy houses,

translation.zh: 把天下的穷苦读书人都庇护起来，让他们都开开心心，
translation.en: to shelter all the poor scholars in the world and make them all smile,

translation.zh: 任凭风吹雨打，房子都像山一样安稳！
translation.en: houses that stand firm as mountains, not shaken by wind or rain!

translation.zh: 唉！
translation.en: Ah!

translation.zh: 什么时候眼前能出现这样高高的房子，
translation.en: When will such tall houses rise up before my eyes?

translation.zh: 就算只有我的茅屋破了，我被冻死，也心甘情愿！
translation.en: Then even if only my hut were broken, and I froze to death, I would be content!

background.zh: 唐肃宗乾元二年（759年）年底，杜甫为了躲避安史之乱，来到成都。第二年春天，在朋友的帮助下，他在城西浣花溪边盖了一座茅草屋，就是后来有名的“杜甫草堂”。上元二年（761年）八月，一场大风刮破了茅屋，接着又下了一夜大雨。杜甫一家又冷又湿，一夜没睡。他写下这首诗，记下了这一夜。
background.en: At the end of 759, Du Fu came to Chengdu to escape the An Lushan Rebellion, a long civil war. The next spring, with help from friends, he built a thatched hut by the Huanhua Stream west of the city. It later became the famous Du Fu Thatched Cottage. In the eighth month of 761, a strong wind tore the roof apart, and then heavy rain fell all night. Du Fu's family was cold and wet and could not sleep. He wrote this poem about that night.

author_note.zh: 杜甫（712—770），字子美，唐代伟大的诗人，被称为“诗圣”。他经历了唐朝从繁荣走向战乱的过程，一生贫困，到处漂泊。他的诗写了很多百姓的苦难，被称为“诗史”，意思是用诗写成的历史。这首诗里，他自己受苦，心里想的却是天下的穷人。
author_note.en: Du Fu (712–770) was one of the greatest Tang poets, called the Sage of Poetry. He lived through the time when the Tang dynasty fell from wealth into war. He was poor and moved from place to place all his life. His poems show the suffering of ordinary people, so they are called 'history in poems'. In this poem he is suffering himself, yet he thinks of all the poor people in the world.

appreciation.zh: 这首诗像一部短短的电影，分四幕。第一幕：大风刮跑屋顶的茅草，茅草飞过江，挂在树上，掉进水塘。第二幕：村里的孩子抱走茅草，老人追不上，只能拄着拐杖叹气。第三幕：天黑了，下起大雨，被子又冷又破，屋里到处漏水，一家人熬着长夜。前三幕都是写自己的苦。到了第四幕，诗人忽然把眼光从自己身上移开，想到天下所有没有房子住的穷人。他希望有千万间结实的大房子，让大家都笑起来；只要这样，就算自己冻死也愿意。从一间小茅屋，想到整个天下，这就是杜甫被称为“诗圣”的原因。
appreciation.en: This poem is like a short film in four scenes. Scene one: a great wind blows the thatch off the roof. It flies over the river, catches in trees and falls into ponds. Scene two: village boys carry the thatch away. The old man cannot catch them and can only lean on his stick and sigh. Scene three: night falls and heavy rain comes. The quilt is cold and torn, water leaks everywhere, and the family waits through the long night. The first three scenes are about his own pain. In scene four, the poet suddenly looks away from himself. He thinks of all the poor people who have no home. He wishes for millions of strong houses so everyone could smile. If that came true, he would be willing to freeze to death himself. From one small hut, he thinks of the whole world. That is why Du Fu is called the Sage of Poetry.
